Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. # - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.

payload.instruction: Stuffing the paper into the cup
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Is the source paper visibly stuffed inside the source cup in the edited image?
node.criteria: Pass if the edited image shows the paper from the source image placed inside the cup from the source image, with visible evidence it has been stuffed into it. Fail if the matched paper and cup are assessable and the paper is visibly outside the cup or only resting nearby or on its rim. Unknown if the source objects cannot be reliably matched in the edited image, or their relationship cannot be assessed.
node.binding: Identify the requested paper and cup by their visual and contextual roles in the source image, allowing their appearance to change in the edited image. Judge whether that paper is stuffed inside that cup; do not require exact color or shape matches.

node_traces.evidence: The source paper and cup are visible, but the edited image shows a hand holding a blue printed item near a round object. The source paper and cup cannot be reliably matched to these objects, so whether the paper was stuffed into the cup cannot be established.

fulfillment: The node’s binding is too abbreviated and leaves the evaluator to infer what counts as the requested paper and cup. Make the binding explicitly preserve the instruction’s entities and action, and require reliable source-to-edit identity matching before crediting either completion or progress. Here the edited image shows a hand holding a blue printed item near a round object; it does not visibly establish that these are the source paper and cup. The support-2 claim of partial progress therefore conflicts with its own unresolved identity evidence and should not be treated as grounded progress. Keep the rubric’s distinction between complete stuffing, genuine partial progress, and no progress; do not turn uncertainty into “no.” The reference label is an aggregate constraint, not proof that the edit is absent. Investigate the support routing/criteria so unresolved matching cannot be overridden by an unsupported progress claim, while retaining unknown when evidence remains insufficient. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is reported; this is a visual grounding and decision-consistency issue.

Make the node explicitly assess whether the source paper and source cup can be reliably matched in the edited image, allowing appearance changes but requiring visual/contextual evidence rather than assuming identity. In this example, the edited image shows a hand-held blue printed item near a round object; the trace calls these the matched paper and cup without explaining the identity evidence. That makes its partial-progress claim inconsistent with unresolved matching. Clarify the criterion or routing so uncertain identity or placement remains unknown, while retaining the distinction between genuine partial progress, no progress, and completion. Do not force the aggregate reference label to mean no progress. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is indicated; investigate visual grounding and decision consistency.
